headline: Slab, screw and Clutch City were made here, and Houston wants the credit
summary: Houston sees itself as the biggest city nobody gave credit to: no zoning, no pretension, one of America's most diverse metros. It gave the world slab, screw and a hip-hop canon built outside New York and LA. Pride runs through the wards, the Southwest corridors and the 1994 and 1995 titles. Speak that dialect: candy paint, purple, chrome, wood grain, the 713.

insights.title: Houston built its culture outside the coastal gaze
insights.detail: Screw music, slab cars and the Third Coast sound grew out of Southside and Third Ward neighborhoods with little industry help. Locals wear that independence as pride. The chip on the shoulder comes from being underrated, overlooked and then copied.
insights.implication: Keep the tone earned and insider, not a Texas-themed tourist pitch. Credit the local originators in product stories instead of borrowing the look.

insights.title: Slab culture is a complete design language
insights.detail: Candy paint, chrome or gold wheels (the poppin' trunk, swangas and elbows), wood-grain steering wheels, vogue tires and the slow, low drive all say Houston. A slab is personal expression and neighborhood status.
insights.implication: Build a Houston colorway and material story on candy-pearl gradients, chrome and gold hardware, wood-grain trim and tire-tread details.

insights.title: Slow and syrupy is the tempo
insights.detail: DJ Screw's slowed-down mixtapes from Southside Houston, the Screwed Up Click, purple drank imagery and the 'slow, loud and bangin' ethos made tempo a local trademark. Houston still hears its sound as its own, with a line running to Swishahouse, UGK, Geto Boys, Travis Scott and Megan Thee Stallion.
insights.implication: Use tempo and blur as graphic ideas: stretched type, echo outlines, tape-cassette references. Handle drug imagery carefully, and work with purple and tape, not cups.

insights.title: Third Ward and Fifth Ward are heritage anchors
insights.detail: Third Ward holds Emancipation Park, Project Row Houses, Texas Southern University and the University of Houston, and is Beyonce's hometown. Fifth Ward is home to the Geto Boys lineage, Frenchtown history and a deep Juneteenth tradition. It shares that tradition with Houston's other historic Black wards, including Freedmen's Town in the Fourth Ward.
insights.implication: Build neighborhood graphics (ward names, area codes) with local artists and community orgs. Credit and pay them. Don't lift the shorthand.

insights.title: Diversity is the actual identity
insights.detail: Alief, Sharpstown and Gulfton, Hillcroft's South Asian district, Bellaire Boulevard's Chinatown and Vietnamese communities, Nigerian and Salvadoran networks, and old Tejano roots all sit inside one city. Houstonians call this the real Houston, more than oil or cowboys.
insights.implication: Show a mosaic of neighborhoods, not one Houston. Collaborations and community events in Southwest Houston can reach a young, multilingual Rockets audience that national campaigns miss.

insights.title: Space City is shorthand, Clutch City is the heart
insights.detail: NASA's Johnson Space Center and the astronaut story gave Houston its Space City nickname. The Hakeem Olajuwon-led 1994 and 1995 championships and the 'Clutch City' label gave the Rockets an underdog-triumph story. Yao Ming and James Harden-era memories layer on top.
insights.implication: Space imagery is easy and overused, so pair it with Clutch City grit and Hakeem's footwork stories. Retro Rockets red, gold and the throwback look in this season's uniform news make a strong nostalgia lane.

insights.title: Weather and survival shape the self-image
insights.detail: Harvey in 2017 and the February 2021 freeze are core civic memories, and 'Houston Strong' became a shared slogan. Heat and humidity run most of the year, so people dress light, breathable and layered against aggressive air conditioning.
insights.implication: Make lightweight, moisture-managing product the core. Treat resilience stories with respect, not as marketing material.

places.name: Project Row Houses
places.why: A long-running Black-led arts and neighborhood initiative on shotgun houses, central to how Third Ward tells its own story.

places.name: Emancipation Park
places.why: Formerly enslaved Houstonians founded it for Juneteenth celebrations, and it is still the holiday's symbolic heart in the city.

places.name: Texas Southern University
places.why: A major HBCU with a famed marching band and deep community ties.

places.name: The Orange Show Center for Visionary Art
places.why: A hand-built folk art environment at the center of Houston's outsider, eccentric DIY art identity. It also organizes the Art Car Parade.

places.name: The Beer Can House
places.why: A house covered in flattened cans, and a fair picture of Houston's anything-goes, self-made visual culture.

places.name: Houston Chinatown on Bellaire Boulevard
places.why: A sprawling Asian American commercial corridor of Vietnamese, Chinese and Korean businesses that shows Houston's suburban-scale diversity.

places.name: Hillcroft Avenue South Asian district
places.why: A dense stretch of South Asian shops, restaurants and community life, and a core part of Southwest Houston identity.

places.name: Toyota Center
places.why: The Rockets' home, in the middle of downtown and the destination for every game-day ritual.

places.name: Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo at NRG Park
places.why: Cowboy culture, Black trail rider tradition, Tejano music and big-name concerts overlap here each spring.

people.name: DJ Screw
people.role: late DJ and originator of chopped and screwed music
people.why: The founding figure of Houston's slowed-down sound. The Screwed Up Click he led is still revered.

people.name: Hakeem Olajuwon
people.role: Rockets Hall of Famer and two-time champion
people.why: The face of the 1994 and 1995 Clutch City titles, and a Nigerian-born symbol of Houston's immigrant heritage.

people.name: Yao Ming
people.why: Opened Houston to Chinese and Asian fandom, and still ties the Rockets to the city's Asian communities.

people.name: Beyonce
people.why: Houston's biggest cultural export. Locals reference her Black Texan heritage with great pride.

people.name: Travis Scott
people.role: Houston-area rapper and founder of Cactus Jack
people.why: A Missouri City native whose brand ties streetwear to Houston. Nike already has a long relationship with him.

people.name: Megan Thee Stallion
people.why: A Houston artist who repped Southside and Hot Girl culture and put Houston's female voice at the center of national rap.

people.name: Bun B
people.why: A widely respected elder voice who regularly speaks for Houston hip-hop history and food culture.

people.name: Paul Wall and Slim Thug
people.why: Paul Wall's grills and Slim Thug's Boss Hogg Outlawz standing embody the grill, candy-paint and slab aesthetic.

moments.name: Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo
moments.why: The city's biggest style moment, with boots, hats, trail rides and concerts across Black, Latino and Anglo communities.

moments.name: Juneteenth celebrations
moments.why: Third Ward and Fifth Ward have long held the holiday as a city-defining Black heritage moment.

moments.name: Art Car Parade
moments.why: A celebration of customized vehicles that only Houston would throw, and an echo of slab culture's DIY spirit.

moments.name: Clutch City anniversary and Finals memories
moments.why: The 1994 and 1995 titles were won in June, so June suits retro Rockets stories.

moments.name: Lunar New Year in Chinatown
moments.why: A major Southwest Houston community moment, and a real way in to Asian Houston and Yao Ming's legacy.

moments.name: Rockets home opener and Cup Nights
moments.why: The opening weeks of the season, including Cup group play against DEN, PHX, DAL and UTA, are the first launch window.

moments.name: MLK Day Rockets game
moments.why: Houston plays Memphis on the national MLK Day slate, a natural moment for Black Houston heritage stories.

moments.name: Hurricane season
moments.why: A defining backdrop to civic identity. Handle storm references with care.

vocabulary.meaning: The classic Houston nickname. Locals use it fondly, and it is a fixture of rap history.
Houston's NASA-derived nickname, used in team branding and local media.
The nickname born of the 1994 title run, still a rallying cry for Rockets fans.
The metro's area codes. 713 is the original and most revered, and people flash them in graphics and hand signs.
A customized car, usually slow, loud and bright, with candy paint and distinctive wheels.
Protruding wire wheels and pop-out elbow-style rims that define classic slab looks.
Houston's take on "man," common in local speech and lyrics.
A word UGK popularized, meaning true and real.

designCues.cue: Rockets red, deep and slightly warm
designCues.source: Rockets primary color and the legacy of Clutch City
designCues.use: Make it the anchor color across Houston apparel, paired with chrome or silver accents.

designCues.cue: Candy-paint purple with a pearl shift
designCues.source: Slab and screw culture, including the purple visual language around Houston music
designCues.use: Use it as a gradient or accent on jackets, shoes and graphics. Avoid cup or drug imagery.

designCues.source: Slab wheels, grills and Houston jewelry culture
designCues.use: Use reflective or metallic prints and hardware, not literal car imagery.
Apply it to trims, labels or a limited jacket lining as an insider nod.

designCues.cue: Stretched, slowed lettering and echo outlines
designCues.source: The slowed-down aesthetic of chopped and screwed music
designCues.use: Use it for wordmarks and graphic tees that suggest tempo without referencing drugs.
Run it as a numerical graphic on caps and tees, with 713 as the hero.

designCues.cue: Bayou green and Gulf humidity haze
designCues.source: Buffalo Bayou and the Gulf Coast
designCues.use: Use it as a supporting color for lightweight warm-weather pieces.

designCues.cue: Ketchup and mustard throwback red and gold
designCues.source: The retro Rockets look reported for this season
designCues.use: Tie nostalgia products to community memories and a verified uniform direction.

productHooks: A 713 capsule: candy-purple gradient, chrome details and an area code graphic, co-designed with a Houston slab and screw artist.
A rodeo-season pack of breathable western-yoked shacket, bucket hat and boot-friendly joggers in Rockets red and gold.
A Clutch City heritage collection built from 1994 and 1995 imagery and Hakeem footwork graphics. Line up licensing with the Rockets and the NBA.
A Juneteenth and Third Ward heritage release, designed with and paid to local Black artists. Give a share of proceeds to local community organizations.
A Southwest Houston diversity capsule celebrating Alief and Sharpstown, with multilingual graphics by local creators.
watchouts: Drug references: purple drank imagery is tied to real harm and to DJ Screw's death. Use purple and tape motifs only.
Make Third Ward and Fifth Ward graphics with community artists. Don't lift from local murals or Project Row Houses artworks without permission.
Rockets, NASA, Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo and Astros marks need licensing. Skip generic NASA or Space City imagery that implies endorsement.
Hurricane Harvey and the 2021 freeze are painful civic memories. Don't frame disaster commercially.
Don't treat Houston as one monolith or reduce it to cowboy hats and oil.
